topic: How Audient's third-generation iD interfaces use RoomTune to measure room acoustics and adjust monitor playback, while onboard DSP handles input effects.
title: Can Your Room Trick Your Violin Mix?
hook: Your room can quietly mislead your mix.
description:
Your room can colour what you hear while mixing. Audient's third-generation iD interfaces add RoomTune monitor correction, which measures room acoustics and adjusts the signal sent to your speakers. Their onboard DSP also runs EQ, compression and reverb without using your computer's CPU. This is monitor correction and input processing, not a change to the original violin recording.

Sources:
MusicRadar: https://www.musicradar.com/music-tech/this-isnt-a-spec-refresh-its-a-completely-new-technology-platform-audient-launches-next-generation-of-id-audio-interfaces-with-onboard-dsp-and-built-in-monitor-correction
Mixdown: https://mixdownmag.com.au/news/room-correction-comes-to-every-model-in-audients-redesigned-id-range/
cover_payoff: Use a short sampled violin phrase as a familiar listening reference while the final scene returns to a fully modelled violin and bow. Keep the room-response diagram conceptual: do not invent measured room data or imply that Prince recorded the sample live.
narration_script: Your room can quietly mislead your mix. Audient's new interfaces combine console-style preamps with onboard digital processing. RoomTune measures room acoustics and adjusts the signal reaching your monitors. Its onboard DSP runs EQ, compression, and reverb without burdening your computer.

narration_evidence.quote: Audient has unveiled the next generation of its iD series of audio interfaces, built on what the company is calling the Analogue Intelligence platform, bringing together Audient’s analogue mic preamps with onboard DSP, monitor correction and new tone-shaping tools.

It measures your room and adjusts the signal going to your monitors to compensate for its acoustics, with the correction stored on and run from the interface’s DSP, so it applies to everything coming out of the speakers rather than only inside a DAW.
The onboard DSP that handles RoomTune also runs hardware-accelerated effects, letting you apply EQ, compression and reverb to input signals with no latency without using your CPU.
